title: Inquest clears police in fatal 2010 shooting
article: A provincial court inquest has cleared two Winnipeg police officers in the fatal shooting of a suspect that occurred almost eight years ago.

Provincial Judge Cynthia Devine ruled Monday that the actions of the two officers were justified and made no recommendations that could have prevented a similar death in the future or identified any deficiencies in training and policies in the inquiry's final report.

At just before 9 a.m., on May 9, 2010, officers responded to a break and enter at a Langside Street residence in West Broadway where they encountered a suspect who had broken into a house armed with a crowbar. The inquest found that the suspect had jumped into a stolen vehicle and tried to run down the officers in an attempt to flee.
Lance Muir, 42 of Winnipeg, was taken to the Health Sciences Centre by ambulance and pronounced dead later the same morning. The cause of death was a gunshot wound to the chest.

The inquest proceedings was delayed to allow for Winnipeg police Homicide Unit to conduct an investigation and for the RCMP to conduct an independent review of the investigation. As a result of the investigation and independent review, no criminal charges were deemed to be warranted.

In an official statement, the Winnipeg Police Service acknowledged a thorough examination of the incident by Judge Devine has confirmed that their members acted appropriately in accordance with policy and training, and that the discharging of a firearm "was justified and appropriate, and entirely in line with police policy and training." "No police officer wants to be involved in a lethal force encounter, but the WPS agrees with Her Honour's assessment that our use-of-force training gives members the techniques they need to address these dangerous situations as safely as possible," the statement read.
While happy with the result, the head of the police association was concerned that it took almost eight years after the incident for the inquest to be completed.
